Article Title: 'Can't die like this': Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recalls flydubai flight ordeal
Article Text:
Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar in hospital

Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, who survived an assault by his Omani co-pilot aboard a flydubai flight in September, recalled the ordeal and how he might not survive.In a teaser released by Sky News Arabia ahead of an exclusive interview, asked whether there was a moment when he thought he might not make it, Machchhar said he told himself he needed to act before it was too late. "I mean, I'm trying to get over it now, but yes, there was a moment that I realised, and I told myself that, Smith, do something. You can't die like this," he said."I'm not saying I accepted my death. It was like, do something, otherwise..." he added, describing the moment when he realised that he had to act.Machchhar also recalled the scene after the cockpit door was opened, describing the panic and screaming. "I remember being face down, and of course the panic which was there, the screaming which was there," he said.He also praised the colleague who took over the controls during the crisis, calling the colleague's actions commendable. "It's something that I'll keep with me till I die," Machchhar said.The interview comes weeks after the September 30 incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The Indian captain was allegedly attacked by his Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, inside the cockpit.Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to intervene and overpower the alleged attacker. The aircraft experienced a sharp drop in altitude before it was brought under control and diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely.The full interview is scheduled to air on Sky News Arabia at 9 pm Abu Dhabi time or 10.30pm IST (5 pm GMT).
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his Omani co-pilot. He managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to overpower the alleged attacker. The interview comes weeks after the September 30 incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073.

Article Title: 'Do something. You can’t die like this': flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchar recounts cockpit attack
Article Text:
'It went on like a normal day till it wasn’t,' Smit recalled

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Two hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Avivi, flydubai commander, Capt Smit Machchar was checking landing time and fuel figures on the computer when something struck hard at the back of his head. He thought part of his Boeing 737’s cockpit roof had broken loose. Seconds later, as more blows rained in, he turned and saw it was his co-pilot. Bleeding, his vision shrunk to a few inches, he drifted in and out of consciousness during those fateful minutes when the aircraft went into a rapid descent, while the attack continued. “There was a moment I told myself, Smit, do something, you can’t die like this,” said the flydubai pilot, recounting the Sept 30 terror attack on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which was diverted and landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. In his first extended account since the incident, given to Sky News Arabia on Sat evening, Machchar said an ordinary flight, with a co-pilot he was flying with for the first time, turned violent minutes after the man stood up to pray.It was a route he had flown many times. An augmented crew was on board, and the relief captain was to take over operating duties after landing.“Normal flight,” he told the channel. “It went on like a normal day till it wasn’t.”About two hours in, the relief captain had dropped by the cockpit to chat about rosters and flying hours when the co-pilot, who had stepped out for a toilet break, returned. A few minutes into their conversation, he said he wished to pray and asked the relief captain to step out. Machchar said such requests are accepted in the region when the flight is stable.The co-pilot asked the other Captain to step out, stood up behind him and began praying. “Out of respect, I did not look back. I was checking the landing time and fuel figures on the computer, the routine background tasks of the monitoring pilot. Suddenly there was a very hard hit at the back of my head,” he said. “It was something very strong and hard. I didn’t know at that point what had hit me.” He fell forward, and his mind reached for training. “My first thought was, okay, something has broken from the aircraft roof, and it has been a catastrophic damage. I was planning to regain my composure and check my systems.”The blows kept coming. Within seconds his vision had narrowed to a few inches, he said. When he glanced back, he understood. “He was saying something while hitting me, but I could not understand.” Machchar unbuckled and tried to shield himself, taking a blow on his hand. “That’s when something flipped,” he said. He screamed for the relief captain and, since the door switch was within reach, managed to open it. He lost consciousness for the first time soon after. He recalled hearing shouting between the co-pilot and the other crew before the door shut again, with the co-pilot threatening to hit them too.It was after this, he said, that he heard the engines spool down and felt the aircraft pitch into a dive. “I don’t have to see the instruments, I can have my eyes closed and still know the engines are spooling down and the aircraft is going down. Every pilot will tell you this.”Drifting in and out of consciousness from blood loss, he said, he reached a point of decision. “I told myself, Smit, do something. You can’t die like this. I’m not saying I accepted my death. It was like, do something, otherwise...” The pilot added his memory of what followed is fragmentary, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. He said he remembers locking his legs against something and pushing toward the door. He said he remembers then lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, the door open, passengers panicking.Machchar credited his colleague for taking the controls and recovering the aircraft, calling it something he will carry “till I die.” Asked about the speculation over how the plane was saved, he declined to single anyone out.“Everyone did the best in their capacity,” he said, including crew and passengers.He said he knew he was out of danger only when the aircraft touched down. Until then a doctor on board and his crew kept him conscious. “At that point, what I was more focused on was to not give up on life. You say you see flashes and stuff like that (speaking about death). You just remember the person who matters the most,” he said. The first call he made was to his 2-year old son. In the days that followed the incident, he continued to get flashes of the first blow. The commander added that he has been getting better with each passing day and can now sit and have conversations.
Article Summary: Capt Smit Machchar was on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Two hours into the flight he was hit hard at the back of his head. He thought part of his Boeing 737’s cockpit roof had broken loose. The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented.

Article Title: Legal profession is not for faint-hearted: CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Two months after students of National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, opposed his presence on the campus, CJI Surya Kant addressed them at the convocation ceremony and said the legal profession is not for the faint-hearted as it demands intellectual independence coupled with fairness and hearing a person before judging.Delivering the ‘Presidential address of the Chancellor’ on Saturday at the convocation, which was postponed after students and alumni of NLSIU opposed his presence, CJI Kant said the university, regarded as ‘Harvard of the East’, has “witnessed its fair share of quad parties and impromptu flash mobs in the courtyard!” Shifting to the serious task, he said the legal profession demands not only the mastery of statutes but also the courage to defend what is just, and the humility to listen to the voices that get drowned in cacophony.CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU said legal profession demands humility to listen to the voices that get drowned in cacophony.“This intellectual independence also calls for fairness: hearing before judging, distinguishing a person from a position and disagreeing without denying another person’s dignity,” he said.He said the purpose of legal education is to enable law graduates to explore the situations beyond criminal and constitutional laws and gain experience from myriad real-life situations where many comprehend the world very differently than ourselves.“Law will challenge your patience, test your ethics, and call upon the deepest reserves of your courage. But it will also reward you with the singular joy of service – the serene satisfaction of righting a wrong, the pride of defending liberty, and the honour of upholding the Constitution,” he said.Advising the students on the challenges that lie ahead of them in the challenging legal profession, the CJI said, “As you leave this campus, you step not only into a profession but into a calling.”
Article Summary: Two months after students opposed CJI Surya Kant’s presence at the campus, he attended the convocation along with Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar in Bengaluru. He said the legal profession is not for the faint-hearted as it demands intellectual independence coupled with fairness.

Article Title: 'Nine murders' claim, then a clarification: How 'Chhote Sarkar' has put Nitish, JD(U) on the spot
Article Text:
Anant Singh is no ordinary legislator as locals rarely use his given name. They call him 'Chhote Sarkar'.

In 2004, Anant Singh weighed Nitish Kumar against silver coins during a public rally in the Barh parliamentary constituency to show his support.

Fate tied to bahubali brother

Pet lover who loves python

Anant Singh with his horses

Jail, raids and remarkable run at the polls

The fluid loyalty

A fragile equilibrium

NEW DELHI: Anant Singh , Bihar's bahubali MLA, who is intensely popular on social media reels for his impromptu one liners in local Magahi dialect, made a jittering claim to prove his loyality and sacrifice for JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar "I got nine people murdered," he said on camera, reviving the distressing memory of Jungle Raj that once besieged Bihar. The statement also had a dramatic irony as he was mentioning the man who ruled Bihar as 'Sushasan Babu', Nitish Kumar.Speaking to reporters about his years of loyalty with Bihar's former chief minister Nitish Kumar, the six-time legislator said: “Who has made so many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then; he used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered.”However, maybe after releasing the political gravity of his remark, the Mokama MLA backtracked and pinned the blame on Lalu Yadav, who was once an ally of Nitish Kumar.The video went viral and the timing was fatal, because Singh, popular as 'Chhote Sarkar', is already at odds with his party over the Patna Graduates’ MLC election.He is backing the candidate fielded by Prashant Kishor against JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar, the very man he defeated in the 2015 assembly election.As criticism came crashing in from the party and the opposition, Singh sensed the backlash and tweaked his remark, saying: “During the Lalu Prasad regime, nine of my associates were killed, and I myself was shot. It was because we aligned ourselves with Nitish Kumar that Lalu had them killed. We have suffered such immense losses. My father also passed away due to a heart attack.”However, the RJD held back the attack as Lalu's party spokesperson Shakti Singh Yadav, said: “Anant has publicly confessed to killing nine persons during the NDA regime. Now Nitish will have to offer explanations.”He went further: “Although he (Anant) has confessed to his involvement in nine murders, the responsibility straightaway goes to Nitish regime...Is paap se chhutkara nahin milekga (There will be no escape from this sin).”Anant Singh is no ordinary legislator as locals rarely use his given name. They call him 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s.His story begins with his elder brother, Dilip Singh. Dilip won as an independent and became a minister in Lalu Prasad’s cabinet during its first term, from 1990 to 1995. Dilip Singh is remembered as the first of the so-called bahubalis, or musclemen politicians, to reach such a post.Anant Singh, who first handled his brother’s election campaigns, took over the family's political reins following Dilip Singh's electoral defeat to rival strongman Surajbhan Singh in 2000.In the next election cycle in 2005, Nitish Kumar, who came to power that year promising to clean up one of India’s poorest and most fractured states, brought Anant Singh into the JD(U). Anant Singh's backing could help the party among upper castes, who did not naturally support Nitish Kumar.However, his allegiance to Nitish began a year before. In 2004, Anant Singh weighed Nitish Kumar against silver coins during a public rally in the Barh parliamentary constituency to show his support.Anant Singh successfully contested the Mokama assembly seat in 2005 on a JD(U) ticket.Once asked why he had embraced a man with such a reputation, Nitish Kumar replied, “There are certain compulsions of politics.”Anant Singh then again contested as a JD(U) candidate in 2010, and the relationship lasted until he quit the party before the 2015 polls.Anant Singh keeps a python as a pet, owns an elephant trained to shake hands and rides an antique buggy pulled by expensive horses.Residents describe him holding a durbar where he settles disputes, hears complaints against the police and acts against “miscreants”. Admirers credit him with safer streets and quicker access to services. Critics see a parallel government.Aanant Singh has faced around two dozen serious cases, ranging from murder and kidnapping to conspiracy to kill and the possession of illegal arms. But for years none ended in a conviction, as judges died, officers were transferred and evidence went missing.In his last affidavit he filed in 2025 Bihar elections, he mentioned 28 criminal cases involving undue influence or personation at an election, making preparation to commit dacoity, insult intended to provoke breach of the peace, rioting and armed with a deadly weapon, dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person.In 2015, after he was arrested on murder and kidnapping charges, Nitish Kumar cut him loose. The move was widely read as a gesture to Lalu Prasad Yadav , his old rival turned new partner. Nitish JD(U) had snapped ties with the BJP-led NDA over Narendra Modi being chosen as the PM face.Anant Singh, however, fought the election from jail as an independent. His wife, Neelam, campaigned in his name and called him a “rare diamond”. Interestingly, he won comfortably without stepping onto the campaign trail.The pressure returned in 2019 after police arrested three suspected sharpshooters on 15 July, who allegedly planned to kill a contractor, Bhola Singh, and his brother Mukesh Singh.They reportedly told investigators that Anant Singh had given them the contract. He gave a voice sample to the state forensic science laboratory.Soon afterwards, an AK-47 and hand grenades were recovered from his ancestral house, and he was booked under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, or UAPA. Anant Singh disappeared for nearly a week.“The man, whose name once spelt terror, is now running for cover,” a senior IPS officer said at the time. He eventually surrendered in a Delhi court and alleged a “conspiracy by political forces”, an apparent dig at the JD(U).Nonetheless, Bihar politics is never bereft of bahubalis. And 2020 was different from 2015. Nitish was back with NDA with ever-dominant BJP under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. And RJD, which was by then handled actively by Lalu's son Tejashwi Yadav, forged an alliance with the Congress.This dynamic also shifted the allegiance of Anant Singh, who fought on RJD's ticket and Nitish Kumar's party. Still in jail in 2020, he won with 78,721 votes, about 53 per cent of valid votes cast, by a margin of more than 65,000.In 2021, a special court in Patna sentenced him to 10 years in the arms case, which cost him his seat. Neelam Devi then won the by-election for the RJD, showing that the family’s hold on Mokama had not loosened.Nitish again dumped the BJP in 2022 and returned to the RJD's Mahagathbandhan fold. But nothing much changed for Anant Singh.In February 2024, Nitish Kumar flipped again, leaving the RJD-led alliance for the BJP-led NDA. He won the floor test comfortably with 129 votes, as the opposition walked out. Anant Singh’s wife, Neelam Devi, was one of three RJD MLAs who cross-voted in his favour, a pointed gesture even though the numbers did not depend on it.Months later, Anant Singh stepped out of Patna jail on 15 days of parole in the middle of the Lok Sabha elections. He backed Lalan Singh of the JD(U) in Munger, a sworn enemy whom his wife had challenged on a Congress ticket in 2019. Munger has roughly 3.5 lakh Bhumihar voters, the community to which Singh belongs. The RJD questioned the timing of his release.The most dramatic chapter came during the Mokama assembly contest in 2025. Dularchand Yadav, 76, was murdered while campaigning for a Jan Suraaj candidate. Police arrested Singh, then the JD(U) nominee, in connection with the killing. The NDA responded that, unlike under the Lalu regime, no leader enjoys immunity from legal action.The case revived an old rivalry with Surajbhan Singh, another Bhumihar strongman. Surajbhan began in the LJP, later moved close to the RJD, and saw his own electoral influence shrink after criminal convictions. His wife, Veena Devi, kept the family relevant in nearby seats. The two men have long competed for land, contracts and political dominance.The arithmetic made the stakes plain. Mokama has about 2.9 lakh voters. Bhumihars number roughly 55,000 to 60,000, Dhanuks about 45,000 and Yadavs about 40,000.Muslims and Dalits together make up roughly 30 per cent. A shift of 5 to 10 per cent could move 15,000 to 25,000 votes. The killing of a Yadav campaigner threatened to unsettle backward caste voters, while the Bhumihar vote risked splitting between two powerful figures.Net-net, contrary to Anant Singh' remark, "Chhote Sarkar" has been an ally, an outcast, a prisoner, a convict and a kingmaker, often within a few years. And this time again, he has been vocal against his party's MLC candidate Neeraj Kumar and backing Jan Suraaj's Anuj Kumar Singh.“Nishant (Nitish Kumar's son) should not have campaigned for Neeraj Kumar. Sometimes he is taken to Barh, sometimes some other places, but there are few people to support him,” Anant Singh said, claiming he would “medically treat” Neeraj in the election.
Article Summary: Anant Singh, Bihar's bahubali MLA, made a jittering claim to prove his loyality and sacrifice for JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. Singh is popular as 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s.

Article Title: 'He kept on hitting': Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar reveals what happened mid-flight as he was stabbed
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi

‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this’

‘Everyone did their best’

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival, describing the repeated blows to his head, his attempts to call for help and the moments he lost consciousness as the aircraft went into a dive.after he was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane.In an exclusive 1st news interview after being stabbed, with Sky News Arabia, Captain Smith Machchhar said there had been nothing unusual about the flight until about two hours after take-off. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.Giving out details as he remembered he said, "when I was just in in the checking my computer for the timing and everything, uh suddenly there was a a very hard hit at the back of my head, right here. And uh it was quite hard and felt that it was something which was very strong."He said he initially thought something had broken off the aircraft's roof and hit him, causing catastrophic damage. Drawing on his training, he tried to regain his composure and check the aircraft's systems. “My thought process went on that track, that oh, there is a big damage in the aircraft which has hit me at the back,” he said.But within seconds, he realised he was being attacked. “He kept on hitting,” Machchhar said.He recalled turning around and realising what was happening, although the impact had severely restricted his field of vision.“Immediately, I would say in the next few seconds, my vision was restricted to like few inches,” he said, adding that he learnt about the extent of the impact from doctors later.His first response was to protect himself from further blows. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the attack, sustaining an injury to his hand. “At this point, it was very obvious what was going on,” he said.Machchhar said he immediately tried to get help from another captain who was on board and was expected to operate the return flight. “I was screaming his name and I was trying because the switch was very close to me to open the door. I was trying to just get help in,” he said.He lost consciousness amid the commotion but remembered managing to open the cockpit door. He could hear shouting as the other crew members confronted the co-pilot. “The door shut immediately after that because he threatened to hit them as well,” Machchhar said.By then, he was struggling to stay conscious and could feel his strength fading because of blood loss. Soon afterwards, he heard the engine sounds change and felt the aircraft go into a dive. “Since I’ve been flying for such a long time, I don’t have to see the instruments to figure out or hear the engine to know what’s happening,” he said.Machchhar said he repeatedly drifted in and out of consciousness but realised he had to fight to survive. “There was a moment where I realised and I told myself that, ‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this,’” he said.His memories of what happened next remain fragmented. He recalled trying to reach the door, bracing his leg against something and pushing himself forward.“The next memory that I have is the door’s open and I’m lying between the cockpit and the galley,” he said. He remembered being face down as panic and shouting continued around him.While Machchhar was fighting to survive, another captain took over the controls and helped save the aircraft. “The other thing, how my other colleague who took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die,” he said.Asked what he wanted people to understand about the incident amid speculation over how the plane was saved, Machchhar said everyone on board had done what they could.“I think everyone in world everyone in world did the best in their capacity to save the day,” he said. The pilot said the first blow continued to haunt him in the days after the attack.“Immediately after the event, I used to get flashes of the first hit. And trust me, it shook me up for the first few days,” he said, describing how the memory would return suddenly and leave his heart racing.But what stayed with him most was the determination of those on board. “One thing that I would take away from that day was the determination, the sheer determination of everyone to survive,” he said.Machchhar said he felt out of danger only when the aircraft touched down in Saudi Arabia. By then, a doctor was attending to him in the galley, while crew members worked to keep him conscious.Asked whom he thought of first, he replied: “My son.” His two-year-old son, wife and daughter live with him in the UAE.Machchhar also expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received in Saudi Arabia and after being brought back to the UAE. “From the first day onwards, the way I was taken care of, the way I was brought back to the UAE, even the care that I was given in Saudi is something I would never forget in my life,” he said.Still recovering from the traumatic incident, he said he felt grateful for the care and support he had received over the preceding two-and-a-half weeks.“Grateful is the word I would say right now,” he said.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.

Article Title: Sabarimala temple opens for Thulam month rituals; CM Satheesan offers prayers
Article Text:
The revered Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple was opened on Saturday for the rituals of the Thulam month, drawing numerous devotees eager to pay their respects.

Temple to open for devotees at 5 am on Sunday

Thulam rituals coincide with Mahanavami and Vijayadashami

The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened on Saturday for the Thulam month rituals, with Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan and several other dignitaries visiting the hill shrine to offer prayers.In the presence of Tantri Kandar Brahmadathan, head priest Prasad E D opened the sanctum sanctorum and lit the ceremonial lamp. The sacred fire was then kindled in the Aazhi, located below the 18 holy steps leading to the shrine.According to news agency ANI, Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan, Travancore Devaswom Board President K Jayakumar, Keralam State Police Chief Ravada Chandrasekhar, and MLAs Pazhakulam Madhu and C V Shanthakumar were among those, who arrived at the Sannidhanam to seek the blessings of Lord Ayyappa.Despite persistent heavy rainfall, thousands of devotees gathered at the hill shrine to offer prayers.The temple will open to devotees at 5 am on Sunday, marking the first day of the Thulam month. The selection of the new Melsanthies, or chief priests, for the Sabarimala and Malikappuram temples is also scheduled for the day through a draw of lots.The selection process for the Sabarimala Melsanthi will take place at the Sopanam at 7.30 am, following the Usha Pooja. Sabarimala Special Commissioner R Jayakrishnan and Devaswom commissioner B Sunilkumar will supervise the proceedings.The draw of lots to select the Malikappuram Melsanthi will subsequently be held at the Malikappuram temple.According to officials, this year's Thulam month rituals are particularly significant as the temple has opened during Mahanavami and Vijayadashami after several decades.The temple will close at 10 pm on October 22, following the conclusion of the Thulam month rituals.
Article Summary: Temple to open for devotees at 5 am on Sunday. Thulam month rituals coincide with Mahanavami and Vijayadashami. The selection of the new Melsanthies, or chief priests, for the Sabarimala and Malikappuram temples is also scheduled.

Article Text:

Article Title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
Article Text:
​Before the dhak begins: The money and machinery behind a Durga pujo​

The quiet work before the dhak

The budget

The pandal takes the biggest share

The idol costs a fifth

A theme, decided half a year early

Two months, or more

Six months, one theme, lakhs of rupees

Where the money comes from

The people who are paid

What it costs to raise a Durga Pujo

What the numbers leave out

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Everything, from beginning to end

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the cost of a medium-scale Durga Puja should be capped to keep it accessible? Yes, absolutely! No, let it vary based on demand. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Long before the first beat of the dhak, a Durga Pujo has already been decided, priced and partly built. The goddess arrives in autumn, but the people who bring her to a neighbourhood start months earlier, with a theme, a budget and a list of permissions that must be collected one office at a time.To the crowds who walk through a pandal's gates, a pujo is a few days of colour, light and sound. To the club that puts it up, it is a yearly project that runs on money raised from the neighbourhood, a small circle of skilled craftsmen and a large number of people who all have to be in the right place on the right day. In West Bengal that project is repeated in locality after locality, each with its own ledger.The ledger is not small. A medium-scale pujo costs several lakh rupees, and the biggest share does not go to the idol at the centre of it all. It goes to the structure built around her. Most visitors never see the figures, the deadlines or the people behind them, and that is exactly how the organisers want it. A pujo is meant to arrive as a finished thing.Nirmal, a pujo organiser from West Bengal who has run one for the past 10 years, knows that ledger well. "A medium scale pujo in West Bengal would cost somewhere between 10 to 15 lakhs," he says. "Every year the budget increases as per the market inflation."That second sentence matters as much as the first. A committee that spent a certain amount last year should expect to spend more this year on the same pujo, before it adds a single new ambition. For a club working with money collected from its neighbours, the target keeps moving upward, and the neighbours are asked to keep up with it.Ask him what costs the most and the answer is immediate. "The pandal costs the most," he says. Not the lighting, not the idol, not the food. He puts the pandal at around Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for a medium-scale pujo, which makes it the line the rest of the budget has to work around.Next to the pandal, the idol is a modest line. "Whatever the pandal costs, the idol costs its one-fifth," Nirmal says. For a medium-scale pujo, that works out to around Rs 80,000.It is a striking ratio. The figure at the heart of the festival, the one every visitor has come to see, costs a fraction of the structure that shelters her.Within the idol's cost, the most expensive element is gold. Certain gold items are designated for it, among them an ornament that is given by the club organising the pujo. The ornament comes from the organisers themselves, which makes it a different kind of expense from the rest.A pandal needs a theme, and the theme needs time. "The theme is decided at least six months ago," Nirmal says, meaning at least six months before the pujo. That is a long lead for a festival that lasts only days.Who decides it varies. In some committees, he says, there is a specific person whose sole job is deciding the theme. In others, the pandal makers can decide it too. The choice matters for more than looks, because the budget is also decided through the theme. Once the idea is fixed, the cost of building it can be worked out, and the money follows.This is why the calendar starts so early. A theme chosen six months out leaves room to price the work, find the right artisan and settle the budget before construction begins. By the time the neighbourhood sees the first bamboo go up, the important decisions have already been made.Construction is where the calendar turns uncertain. Asked how long a medium-scale pandal takes to build, Nirmal is candid. "It depends on the workers, to be honest," he says. "Some can build the same pandal in two months, whereas some will require more time."The reason, as he describes it, is a shortage of skill. "The skilled pandal makers are not a lot in number. Mostly there is just one skilled artisan and a lot of people work under him."That structure explains a good deal. The quality of the pandal and the speed at which it rises rest heavily on one person, with a large crew following his lead. For an organiser, choosing a pandal maker is therefore as much a scheduling decision as a financial one. A maker who is slow, or one who is booked elsewhere, can put the whole timeline at risk.The funding model is local. "Every area or colony has a designated club which builds a pandal," Nirmal explains. "And then they get chanda, donations, advertisements that ultimately make the pujo what it is."There is also help from the state. This year, he says, the West Bengal government is providing Rs 1 lakh to small-scale pujos, and electricity is completely free. Free power removes a bill that would otherwise sit beside the lighting and the pandal. The Rs 1 lakh grant, though, is meant for small-scale pujos. Set against a medium-scale budget of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh, most of the money still has to come from the neighbourhood, from donors and from advertisers.Some costs are smaller but just as fixed. The priest's expenditure, Nirmal says, is around Rs 30,000 to Rs 40,000. The dhaki, whose drumming is as much a part of the pujo as the idol, is paid around Rs 10,000. On top of that, he gets free food, lodging and clothes.Those extras are part of the arrangement. A dhaki who is housed and fed for the duration of the pujo is a cost the committee carries beyond the headline fee. Nirmal was also asked about bhog expenditure, but his answer covered only the priest and the dhaki.Add up the lines Nirmal named, the pandal, the idol, the priest and the dhaki, and the total lands somewhere between roughly Rs 4.2 lakh and Rs 6.3 lakh. His estimate for the whole pujo is Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh.The gap is considerable. It covers everything else a pujo needs, including the lighting and food he named only to rule them out as the biggest expense. Nirmal did not break down how that money is divided.Asked about the biggest challenge organisers face, Nirmal does not name a single expense. "The biggest challenge is that everything from the beginning to the end is completed properly," he says.That includes permissions. "You have to get proper permissions like the police and the fire department," he says, "and it takes a lot of people to complete a pujo and to make a pujo what it is."The pandal maker and his crew, the artisan working on the idol, the priest, the dhaki and the club members collecting funds are all working towards the same date. Seen this way, the Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh is only part of what a pujo demands. The rest is coordination, and much of Nirmal's decade in the job has gone into it.For the people who walk through the gates, the pujo arrives as a finished thing. For the club behind it, it began at least six months earlier with a decision about a theme, and it will begin again next year at a higher cost.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: “We could have fought with Verstappen”: Valentino Rossi rues qualifying mistake

Valentino Rossi explains what went wrong

GT World Challenge Europe season finale: Race schedule

Moto GP legend Valentino Rossi was left disappointed after a mistake during qualifying cost him a chance to start close to Max Verstappen at the GT World Challenge Europe event in Portimao, Portugal. The MotoGP legend had set a competitive lap time and believed he could have been in a strong position on the starting grid. However, his lap was deleted for exceeding track limits, leaving him without a valid time. Rossi said the result was frustrating because he believed he could have challenged Verstappen and his own team's other car.At the GT World Challenge Europe event, the starting grid is decided by the average of each driver's best lap times. During Q1, Q2 and Q3, all three drivers in each car complete flying laps.Valentino Rossi felt his qualifying session had gone well until his lap time was deleted. Speaking to Sky Italia, he explained how the lost time affected his chances."We’re very, very disappointed because the lap had been good, the weather was good, and it would have allowed us to start very close to Verstappen and very close to the #32, our teammates, so it had been a good qualifying session," he said.ID@undefined Caption not available.The Italian said he had tried to stay within track limits at the difficult corners but went slightly wide at Turn 4 while driving close to another car.Valentino Rossi admitted that he had expected to lose some time at risky corners but did not think he would exceed track limits at Turn 4."Honestly, I was expecting it because I had always left myself a little bit of margin in all the risky corners, but at Turn 4, I went over the limit by just a tiny bit. I was close to another car, so I went a little wide, and that meant I exceeded track limits,” Rossi said."The problem was that, since I had set a good lap, I had another lap available, but I was behind another car and slowed down because I thought to myself, ‘I’ve already got a lap time, and I’ll lose time trying to overtake him anyway,” he added.Rossi's decision to slow down proved costly. By the time he learned that his earlier lap had been deleted, he no longer had enough time to set another competitive lap.ID@undefined Caption not available.He was left facing a start near the back of the field. "We were left without a time and will start second-to-last, 60th, something like that," he said.Valentino Rossi believes the lost opportunity was particularly frustrating because he felt he had the pace to start close to Verstappen. "So it’s a shame because we could have fought with Verstappen, as we were right there, and it would have been great.But instead, this is how it’s turned out," he said.Verstappen and his team are scheduled to start the race from 15th on the grid, putting them in a position to fight their way forward during the endurance event.The final endurance race of the GT World Challenge Europe season is scheduled to take place at the Portimao circuit on Saturday.The three-hour race is due to start at 17:00 GMT (18:00 CEST) and finish at around 20:00 GMT (21:00 CEST).While Rossi faces a difficult task after his qualifying setback, Verstappen and his team will aim to make progress from 15th place on the starting grid.Also read: Valentino Rossi net worth: How the nine-time world champion built his $210 million fortune

Article Title: Rio Ferdinand brutally trolled by fans as ‘disgrace’ after “pick up ya t**s” fat-shaming row with Manchester United content creator

The former Manchester United defender was accused of fat-shaming the influencer after responding to criticism of his silence on the club’s ownership.Ferdinand hit back after Saeed TV told him to “Stop yapping and call out the owners!” The former England international replied with a personal comment about Saeed’s weight. His response has since triggered strong reactions from fans, with some calling the remark unacceptable while others defended Ferdinand.The controversy began after Rio Ferdinand shared a picture of himself with Manchester United manager Michael Carrick. He also quoted Carrick, who had recently said, “It is not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player and anyone else who works at the club.”It is unclear exactly why Ferdinand shared the message. The defender reportedly questioned the strength of the squad and made strong comments about the club’s leadership.Saeed TV was unhappy with Ferdinand’s post. He questioned why the former defender had not been more vocal about Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.He commented, “Stop yapping and call out the owners!”Ferdinand responded sharply. Article Title: 'If I were Vinicius, I would have forced an exit from club': Real Madrid coach drops bombshell
Article Text:
UEFA Champions League - AS Roma v Real Madrid - Stadio Olimpico, Rome, Italy - October 14, 2026. Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior looks dejected after AS Roma's Donyell Malen scores their second goal

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that he would have forced an exit from the club last summer if he were in Vinicius Junior's position, pointing to the repeated abuse the Brazilian winger has faced.Vinicius was sent off during Madrid's win over Villarreal last weekend for pulling an opponent's hair. He received a four-match ban as a result and will miss the Clasico against Barcelona on October 25.The 26-year-old has also been regularly targeted by opposition fans and subjected to racial abuse on several occasions since joining Madrid in 2018."He's a spectacular kid who it's easy to have a good relationship with," Mourinho told reporters."He's a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile..."If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn't be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him."Vinicius signed a new contract with Madrid in the summer, extending his stay at the club until 2032.Questions remain over whether Madrid can fit their attacking stars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham into the same team without losing balance."Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed and he keeps on smiling," continued Mourinho."No one or nobody can... well, influence him negatively yes, because he's human... but take away his joy of living and working and being with his team-mates, no, no one can do that."Mourinho substituted Vinicius during Madrid's 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday. The winger is still trying to regain the form that helped him win the competition twice under former coach Carlo Ancelotti.Mourinho also said he was pleased that Vinicius had received a four-match ban, as he had expected the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee to impose a longer suspension."I thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee would give him one or two more," Mourinho said.Madrid will face Sevilla on Sunday as they look to avoid falling further behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday.Barcelona, coached by Hansi Flick, have won every match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Madrid

Article Title: Daniel Dubois fears Fabio Wardley is “gambling with his life” ahead of brutal WBO heavyweight title rematch

Daniel Dubois has expressed serious concerns about Fabio Wardley’s health ahead of their highly anticipated heavyweight rematch. The British boxer believes his rival is taking a major risk by stepping into the ring again after their brutal first encounter in May. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round after surviving two knockdowns in a thrilling contest in Manchester.The rematch will see Dubois defend his WBO heavyweight title against Wardley, who is determined to reclaim the championship. However, Dubois believes the physical cost of boxing is a serious concern and fears another punishing fight could have lasting consequences for his opponent.Speaking on In Camp With, Daniel Dubois explained that he understands why Fabio Wardley accepted the rematch despite the punishment he suffered in their previous meeting.“He has no choice. He probably thinks he has nowhere else to go. It’s a world title fight and he wants to make money- like us all. He was never going to turn it down. He’s going to take another gamble. Fabio is gambling with his health, his life, like we all do. We are prize fighters. This is a sport, but it’s a blood sport”, he said per The Sun.Dubois’ comments reflect the dangers both men face as they prepare to fight again. The two heavyweights have developed powerful reputations, but their first meeting showed how quickly a fight can become dangerous.Wardley made a stunning start in their May contest. He landed a trademark looping right hand just nine seconds into the fight, catching Dubois around the temple. Another powerful right hand in the third round sent the champion to the canvas again.However, Dubois recovered and gradually took control of the contest. His trainer, Don Charles, reportedly gave him a slap around the chops before the fifth round to help him regain his focus.The fight then turned increasingly difficult for Wardley. Dubois landed repeated heavy punches, leaving his opponent with a badly damaged right eye and a bloodied, injured nose. The referee eventually stopped the contest in the 11th round.Dubois believes the damage sustained in such contests can have lasting effects on fighters. He explained that every fight takes something away from a boxer, regardless of the result.“Every fight changes you. Every fight takes a bit out of you. Every time you get in that ring, it takes a little bit out of you. I have to build up this amount of energy and intensity so that I’m just a monster in there. Boxing is a unique sport - it’s not even really a sport”, he said.Despite his concerns, Dubois understands that he must approach the rematch as a professional. He also made it clear that he cannot hold back if Wardley and his team are prepared to continue.The rivals first met in 2017, when they sparred at the Peacock Gym in Canning Town. Since then, both have built successful careers and competed for world titles.
Article Summary: Daniel Dubois warns Fabio Wardley about the risks of their rematch. The British boxer believes his rival is taking a major risk by stepping into the ring again. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round after surviving two knockdowns in a thrilling contest in Manchester.

Article Title: Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement as Eagles star puts mental health first
Article Text:
Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement as Eagles star puts mental health first

The Pivot Podcast

The Pivot Podcast

First Take

Lane Johnson explains his retirement as Ryan Clark defends his decision

Ryan Clark has defended Lane Johnson after Stephen A. Smith questioned the Philadelphia Eagles tackle’s decision to retire during the 2026 NFL season. Speaking on, Clark said that a person’s intentions matter less than the effect their words have on others. He also praised Johnson for putting his mental health and family first, while pointing out why Smith’s comments deserved criticism despite his later apology.Ryan Clark made his position clear while discussing Johnson’s retirement and the reaction to it. He said he was proud of the veteran offensive tackle for choosing what was best for him rather than forcing himself to continue playing football.“Lane Johnson’s football career has been about intent and impact. And I think more people should understand that,” Clark said on. He also welcomed Smith’s apology but stressed that good intentions do not erase the effect a person’s words can have.“Your intent doesn’t matter. It’s about your impact. It’s about what people see in you, how you’ve changed people’s lives,” Clark added.His comments came after Smith faced criticism for the way he discussed Johnson’s decision on ESPN’s. On October 7, one day after the retirement announcement, Smith questioned why Johnson had chosen to walk away when the Eagles were struggling through a difficult stretch of the season.The Eagles were 2-2 at the time and had suffered back-to-back losses. Smith also pointed to the team’s injury problems and the absence of key players, including A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, while questioning Johnson’s timing.During the discussion, Smith repeatedly referred to Johnson’s mental health in a sarcastic tone. That approach drew criticism because Johnson had clearly explained that his emotional well-being and family priorities were behind his decision.Clark’s response focused on the difference between questioning a player’s timing and dismissing the personal reasons behind such a major life choice. For him, Johnson’s decision showed that looking after yourself can matter more than staying in a sport, even when your team still needs you.Lane Johnson announced his retirement on October 6, bringing an end to a 14-season career with the Philadelphia Eagles. The veteran offensive lineman admitted that walking away was difficult, especially because he had hoped to play one more season alongside his teammates.“I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season,” Johnson wrote in his retirement statement.However, he explained that his priorities had changed and that continuing to play was no longer the right choice for him.“Right now it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game,” Johnson said. “And right now my heart is telling me that it’s time to say goodbye to football.”Johnson’s words made it clear that he did not want to continue playing unless he could give the game his full attention. He also wanted to put his family and personal well-being first rather than extend his career for another season.Clark praised that choice, noting that Johnson had previously spoken about protecting his mental health and was now following the same principle in his own life. His message was that stepping away does not make someone weak, even when that person is a physically strong and successful athlete.
Article Summary: Lane Johnson announced his retirement on October 6, bringing an end to a 14-season career with the Philadelphia Eagles. Stephen A. Smith questioned why Johnson had chosen to walk away when the Eagles were struggling through a difficult stretch of the season. Ryan Clark said he was proud of the veteran offensive tackle for choosing what was best for him.

Article Title: 8 dead, 8 injured as mini bus plunges into 15-feet drain on Delhi-Mumbai Expressway near Kota
Article Text:
A bus overturned on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Kota





KOTA: At least eight persons were killed and eight others injured after a mini bus carrying around 23 members of a family from Madhya Pradesh veered off the road and fell into a 15-foot-deep drain along the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway under Simliya police station in Kota district early Saturday morning.The family members departed from Bhopal around 7 pm Friday and headed to Khatu Shyamji temple in Sikar district of Rajasthan. The accident took place around 6 am Saturday.Rescue operations were swiftly launched, though team efforts were severely hampered by mud and accumulated water inside the drain. Emergency personnel deployed cranes at the spot to lift the damaged vehicle and recover trapped individuals.Confirming the details of the ongoing operation, Simliya SHO Nand Singh told TOI that eight bodies have been retrieved from the wreckage so far. He noted that around 23 passengers were on board the traveller bus during the crash.The injured were rushed to nearby medical facilities, including New Medical College Hospital and MBS Hospital in Kota, with three ambulances deployed for quick transportation, the SHO said. Eight injured passengers have been admitted to the two medical facilities for treatment, police said.While official casualties currently stand at eight fatalities, authorities fear the death toll may rise as rescue teams continue to clear the site and verify victim identities.Identities of those killed and injured are yet to be ascertained, along with other details of the passengers, the SHO said.
Article Summary: A mini bus carrying around 23 members of a family from Madhya Pradesh veered off the road and fell into a 15-foot-deep drain along the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway. The family members departed from Bhopal around 7 pm Friday and headed to Khatu Shyamji temple in Sikar district of Rajasthan.

A Cook County sheriff’s officer has sued WWE and wrestler Montez Ford over an alleged unwanted sexualised dance during, claiming the televised incident led to public humiliation and left his children being mocked at school. The lawsuit centres on footage from a July event in Illinois, which the plaintiff says spread online after WWE and Ford shared it.Noel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer who also works private security, was assigned to the July 6, 2026, episode ofat Allstate Arena in Rosemont, near Chicago. According to the lawsuit, a WWE employee instructed him to take a position closer to ringside before the Street Profits’ entrance.The tag-team duo, Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins, were making their way to the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, allegedly approached Lucas and performed an unwanted lap dance during the Netflix broadcast. The complaint says Ford danced immediately in front of and over Lucas, repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis.The lawsuit describes the encounter as “a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.’”It further alleges Ford moved progressively closer to Lucas as the dance continued, with his “left inner thigh repeatedly rub[bing] against Plaintiff’s leg.” The footage appeared to show Lucas looking uncomfortable before later cracking a faint smile, although the lawsuit alleges that the performance was unscripted and took place without his consent.The interaction was not included in the current Netflix replay of the July 6 programme, which cuts to a commercial break early in the Street Profits’ entrance. However, a clip circulated online, including through WWE’s and Ford’s social media accounts. Lucas alleges that the video attracted hundreds of thousands of views and made him recognisable to members of the public.According to the complaint, Lucas encountered people at his full-time courthouse job who recognised him from the clip and mocked him by thrusting their hips towards him, imitating the movements Ford had allegedly performed. The lawsuit also says Lucas’s children were “mocked and ridiculed” at school because of the video.Lucas alleges that he has suffered “humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress” and continues to experience distress because the footage remains publicly available. His complaint also argues that WWE and Ford used his visible image for commercial purposes without authorisation, allegedly violating the Illinois Right of Publicity Act.Lucas filed the lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Cook County, naming WWE, Crawford and its subsidiary Event Services, LLC, as defendants. The complaint lists 14 counts, including allegations of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.The lawsuit seeks unspecified monetary and punitive damages, reimbursement of legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using Lucas’s identity. These are allegations in a civil complaint, rather than findings established by a court.WWE had not immediately responded to a request for comment, according to the report. The case is scheduled for a management hearing on December 10.Lucas’s second job brought him to the arena. Alongside his work for the Cook County Sheriff’s Department, he supervises a team of security guards for Monterrey Security, the private firm that assigned him to the event.In a press release provided to POST Wrestling , Lucas’s attorney Whitney Barr said: “Like so many law enforcement officers, Mr. Lucas works a second job in order to better provide for his children.”Lucas is represented by Barr and Alexis Martin of Caffarelli & Martin Ltd. The lawsuit places the alleged incident, its circulation online and the claimed impact on Lucas’s family at the centre of the dispute, while the defendants’ responses and the court’s findings remain pending.
Article Summary: Noel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer who also works private security, was assigned to the July 6, 2026, episode ofat Allstate Arena in Rosemont, near Chicago. Article Title: In 2026, Gerard Piqué joined India’s FYERS American Gambits after backing Freestyle Chess a year earlier: How the Barcelona legend is building his chess business empire
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO: Gerard Pique attends a press conference in Sao Paulo, Brazil, January 16, 2026. REUTERS/Amanda Perobelli/File Photo

Piqué’s chess investment followed a career built around sporting ventures

He joined FYERS American Gambits as a strategic shareholder

Piqué’s investment arrived as chess pursued wider audiences

American Gambits finished third in Piqué’s first season

The Untold Story of FYERS American Gambits

Gerard Piqué had spent years looking for ways to make sport work differently, even before he retired from football in 2022. Last year, that interest took him into chess, where he invested in Freestyle Chess; in August 2026, he added another stake by joining the FYERS American Gambits as a strategic shareholder. The move brought the former Barcelona defender into a growing business around elite chess, digital audiences, and sporting entertainment, inserting his venture directly into the Tech Mahindra-backed Global Chess League, where the Indian-based franchise competes on a global stage.Piqué retired in 2022 after making 615 official appearances for Barcelona and winning 30 trophies with the club, including three Champions League titles. He also helped Spain win the 2010 World Cup, but his business ambitions had taken shape while he was still playing.In 2017, he founded Kosmos, a sports, media and entertainment company focused on developing new sporting properties and business models. Kosmos later created the Kings League, a seven-a-side football competition featuring shorter matches, unconventional rules, streamers and content creators, with a format designed for digital audiences.Piqué’s interest in chess became public in 2025 through his investment in Freestyle Chess, a venture founded by grandmaster Magnus Carlsen and German entrepreneur Jan Henric Buettner. In July that year, Piqué attended the Freestyle Chess Grand Slam in Las Vegas, where he joined a broadcast with grandmaster David Howell, international master Tania Sachdev and Buettner. He said it was his first top-level chess event.Asked about his favourite player, Piqué answered: “For me, Magnus. I think for everyone. He is a legend.” When asked where Carlsen might play on a football pitch, Piqué joked: “I assume in the midfield because he will move the team all around!”On 17 August 2026, the FYERS American Gambits announced Gerard Piqué’s entry as a strategic shareholder at a press conference in Bengaluru. The Indian-owned professional chess franchise, which is backed by the online stock brokerage firm FYERS, stated that his involvement reflects their ambition to drive the global growth of the sport.Piqué joins an established ownership group that includes Indian cricket star Ravichandran Ashwin, a co-owner since the team’s debut in 2024. The Gambits compete in the Global Chess League, a groundbreaking tournament launched by Tech Mahindra and FIDE. As the world's first franchise-based chess league, it features six international teams competing in a fast-paced, digital-first format. The team’s CEO and co-owner, Prachura P P, described the investment as a landmark moment that perfectly bridges Indian corporate backing with international sports entertainment.“Gerard understands what it takes to build a global sporting property, one that combines elite competition with compelling storytelling, passionate communities and a strong connection with fans,” Prachura said. He added that Piqué’s belief in the franchise’s vision was meaningful as it worked towards building “the future of chess”.The financial terms of Piqué’s investment, including the size of his stake, were not disclosed. His role was presented as a strategic investment rather than a public endorsement, although the franchise did not detail the precise commercial arrangements.The Global Chess League is the competition; FYERS American Gambits is one of its franchises, with FYERS serving as the team’s title sponsor. Piqué’s involvement fits his wider interest in turning established sports into entertainment properties that can reach audiences beyond their traditional fan bases.Freestyle Chess and the Global Chess League approach that ambition differently, but both seek to package elite chess for broader audiences. Piqué’s experience building the Kings League gives him a familiar perspective on digital presentation, fan communities and sports storytelling.He was also part of a growing group of high-profile athletes investing in chess. In March 2026, Manchester City forward Erling Haaland’s investment in the FIDE-approved Total Chess World Championship Tour was reported. The tour is organised by the team behind Norway Chess, which later announced a $10 million funding round featuring Norwegian cross-country skiing star Johannes Høsflot Klæbo, former cycling world champion Thor Hushovd and business investors.Piqué joined the franchise shortly before the fourth season of the Global Chess League, held in Bengaluru from 3 September to 13 September 2026. FYERS American Gambits finished third, securing a podium place behind champions Ganges Grandmasters and runners-up Alpine APL Pipers.The reported season prize fund totalled $1 million, distributed through team standings, game points and a champions’ bonus. The standings-based payouts listed $250,000 for Ganges Grandmasters, $125,000 for Alpine APL Pipers, $75,000 for American Gambits and $50,000 for CheQ Mumba Masters; the champions also received a reported $50,000 bonus, alongside their share of the performance pool.The third-place finish gave the franchise a strong result in the season that followed Piqué’s arrival, although it does not establish the financial return on his investment. The team also featured in, a documentary released on ZEE5.Piqué’s chess portfolio now spans two ventures, with American Gambits adding a team-franchise investment to his earlier involvement in Freestyle Chess. The exact terms remain private, but his move reflects a broader shift among sporting figures who see chess not only as competition, but as a property with room to grow through media, new formats and global audiences.
Article Summary: Gerard Piqué joined FYERS American Gambits as a strategic shareholder in August 2026. The move brought the former Barcelona defender into a growing business around elite chess, digital audiences, and sporting entertainment. The Indian- owned professional chess franchise, which is backed by the online stock brokerage firm FYERS, stated that his involvement reflects their ambition to drive global growth of the sport.

The former UFC light heavyweight champion eventually contacted Cejudo himself after watching one of his breakdowns.According to Cejudo, Jones praised his ability to explain the fighter’s game and gave him a major compliment, “I couldn’t explain myself better than what you did.”That conversation eventually led to Jones visiting Cejudo multiple times.Cejudo has revealed that Jones came to work with him on six different occasions. Their sessions were particularly relevant ahead of Jones’ heavyweight debut against Ciryl Gane at UFC 285 in March 2023.Jones travelled to Phoenix, Arizona, where he worked with Cejudo and coach Eric Albarracin at Fight Ready. The sessions focused on sharpening Jones’ skills and helping him prepare for the challenges of competing at heavyweight.However, Cejudo has always been careful about describing his role in Jones’ development.He did not believe that Jones needed someone to teach him how to fight. Jones had already established himself as one of the greatest fighters in MMA history.Instead, Cejudo viewed his contribution as helping an already elite fighter make small improvements. That is where his famous Lamborghini comparison comes in.For Cejudo, Jones was already a high-end machine. He simply wanted to help polish it and make sure everything was working at the highest possible level.The collaboration also highlighted the respect between two of the most accomplished fighters in combat sports.Cejudo won Olympic gold in wrestling at the 2008 Beijing Games before becoming a UFC champion in two weight classes. Jones, meanwhile, built a legendary career at light heavyweight before moving up to heavyweight and winning the vacant UFC heavyweight title.Cejudo’s own wrestling background made his experience particularly valuable to Jones. The former Olympic champion understood the importance of positioning, pressure, timing and conditioning at the highest level.Cejudo has since continued his own combat sports career. He recently returned to wrestling competition and faced Merab Dvalishvili at RAF 12.While Cejudo now has his own combat sports commitments, his story about Jones shows the level of respect the heavyweight champion had for his technical knowledge.
Article Summary: Henry Cejudo has revealed how Jon Jones personally reached out to him after watching his detailed fight breakdowns. The Olympic gold medallist became known for breaking down fighters and explaining the technical aspects of their games on his YouTube channel. Jones later visited him on six separate occasions to learn and work with him. The sessions focused on sharpening Jones’ skills and helping him prepare for the challenges of competing at heavyweight.
